News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace make decision on Wilfried Zaha transfer as club legend, 33, returns to training as a free agent
Sports.content:
WILFRIED ZAHA is back training at Crystal Palace but will not be rejoining the club.

The club favourite has been back at the club’s Beckenham training base after completing his contract with Galatasaray in Turkey.



Yet Palace currently have no plans to re-sign the Ivory Coast international who played over 400 games for the club.

The 33-year-old still lives in the area, so he is being allowed to train with Palace while he looks for a new club before the start of the season.



Zaha spent the start of this year playing on loan for former Aston Villa manager Dean Smith at Charlotte FC but the parties could not agree on a permanent deal after his Gala contract ended.

The winger made his senior Palace debut in 2010 after coming through the club’s academy.



He went on to play 458 times for the club, either side of a brief stint at Manchester United and a loan at Cardiff – scoring 90 goals and laying on 54 assists.

Zaha departed Selhurst Park on a free transfer in 2023 despite being offered a lengthy extension.

The 36-cap Ivory Coast international opted to instead move to Turkey, going on to win a league title and domestic cup with Galatasaray.

During this period he went out on two loans; an ill-fated short spell at Lyon and with Smith at Charlotte.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Palace, meanwhile, are still looking to recruit a host of players for new boss Pierre Sage.

Dwight McNeil, £21million winger Anan Khalaili and defenders Takehiro Tomiyasu and Oscar Mingueza have joined but a number of other new arrivals are in the pipeline.

Palace lost their final pre-season friendly 3-0 to Freiburg over the weekend.

They will get their new Prem campaign underway this Saturday with a trip to Everton.

Sports.title: ‘It comes as a shock’ – Luke Littler’s pal Angryginge releases sweary rant after being dropped from Sky Sports
Sports.content:
YOUTUBER Angryginge was left baffled after Baller League was dropped by Sky Sports.

It was reported on Monday that Sky decided against renewing its contract with the six-a-side league.



Baller League will continue to be streamed live on YouTube while chief executive Felix Starck looks to find a free-to-air TV deal.

YouTuber and social media star Angryginge, who is the manager of Baller League team Yanited, had not been made aware of the move before it was announced.



On a stream, the 24-year-old, who is close friends with darts superstar Luke Littler, said: “I just saw it. Apparently Baller League has been dropped by Sky Sports.

“I don’t know whether that’s part of the plan or whatnot, I haven’t got a f***ing clue.



“But yeah, that’ll be very, very interesting. I’ve got to say, it comes as a shock, it really does.

“That league, reported to be watched more than the Premier League. Why would Sky Sports drop it?

“It makes no f***ing sense to me. Makes zero sense.

“I mean, there’s more to it than that. There’s more to it that meets the eye probably, I don’t know the ins and outs.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But it could be the end of the road for Yanited, it seems that way.”

The 2025-26 Premier League campaign was Sky Sports‘ most-watched season ever, with viewing figures increased by 25 per cent.

Figures for the latest season of Baller League on the channel are currently unknown.

Those involved with the competition over its first three seasons include KSI, Alan Shearer, Idris Elba, Micah Richards, Gary Lineker, Ian Wright and Chloe Kelly.

Sports.title: Who is Pep Guardiola’s wife Cristina Serra and when did the former Man City manager split with her?
Sports.content:
PEP Guardiola and Cristina Serra called time on their marriage after more than 30 years together at the end of 2024.

In February 2025, the Sun exclusively revealed the couple had begun divorce proceedings — with both of them even using the same lawyer.

Who is Pep Guardiola’s wife Cristina Serra?

Pep Guardiola was married to Brazilian journalist and writer Cristina Serra.



In January 2025, the couple ended their relationship after living apart for years, with Cristina moving back to Barcelona to run her fashion company.



Determined to avoid an ugly court battle and remain on good terms, they made the bold decision to share the same legal team.

The extraordinarily rare “one couple, one lawyer” divorce means the formal end of their marriage will not be contested by either side.

Spanish journalist Lorena Vazquez, who broke the story of their split, explained: “They want it above all to be friendly for the sake of their children.



“As you can imagine money is not going to be an issue and they have already agreed the initial terms to make sure this separation is the most cordial possible.

“They have a very good relationship, so much so that the same lawyer is arranging the whole thing.

“The divorce is on the way and is being left in the hands of people with their absolute trust.”

She told Spanish TV programme Y Ahora Sonsoles that the couple ended things after Pep signed a two-year extension — keeping him at the Etihad until at least 2027.



Cristina’s family owns fashion store Serra Claret in Barcelona, where she met her future husband when he was just 18 years old.

Pep was doing some modelling for designer Antonio Miro in the shop when he first saw Cristina.

Serra Claret stocks many brands that you see Pep wearing on the touchline including Dsquared2, CP Company and Armani.

Pep previously stated that he trusts his wife so much when it comes to fashion that he lets her pick his clothes for him.

In an interview in January 2024, the footie boss revealed how Cristina even chose his match day outfits.



They want it above all to be friendly for the sake of their children Lorena Vazquez ,

Speaking to Men In Blazers, he said: “My wife is the best in the world at many things, but especially in fashion.

“So she says normally to me, don’t wear this or wear that, so I follow her.

“I am smart enough to know that when people are much, much better than me, follow their advice, and hers is really good.”

When did Pep Guardiola and Cristina Serra get married?

Despite the Manchester City boss meeting his wife as a teenager, they waited a long time to get married.

The pair wed in 2014 in an intimate ceremony in Spain.



They had a private service for close family in the beautiful Spanish area of Catalonia.

Do Pep Guardiola and Cristina Serra have children?

The couple have three children, Maria, Marius and Valentina.

Their eldest daughter Maria is a model who has over 925K followers on Instagram as of February 25, 2025.

She has been very vocal about her love of Man City, a club that dad Pep feels completely at home with.



In 2021, Maria was spotted with ex-Spurs ace Dele Alli in a romantic clinch.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A few months later, they were seen getting lunch together at trendy Mayfair hotspot Novikov, before grabbing a coffee at Starbucks.

However, six months later it was reported that Dele had split with Maria.

Sports.title: Why Enzo Fernandez to Man City is not as simple as it seems despite transfer for £120m Chelsea star suiting both clubs
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are ready and willing to sell Enzo Fernandez.

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca would love to be reunited with the midfielder he brought the best out of when he was in charge of the Blues.





And Fernandez himself has made no secret of his desire to leave Stamford Bridge.

But just because a deal would appear to suit all parties, does not mean it will happen.

And if Fernandez does move to the Etihad in this transfer window, negotiations are likely to go down to the wire.

Why? Because Chelsea and City have both made their stances crystal clear and are now in a Mexican stand-off. Or an Argentinian stand-off, if you prefer.

Neither will want to blink first. Especially because the relationship between the two clubs is already strained by the way Maresca left Stamford Bridge and then pitched up in Manchester as Pep Guardiola’s replacement.

It is not just players and agents and managers who have egos.

Club owners and executives do, too. Chelsea and City do not want to lose face and let the other side “win” in the battle over Fernandez’s future.

Neither club is willing to go on the record in the same way as, say, Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin.





He pinned his colours firmly to the mast way back in June when he said star forward Julian Alvarez would be going nowhere and criticised Barcelona’s pursuit of Fernandez’s Argentina team-mate.

It is a stance Gil Marin and Atletico head coach Diego Simeone maintain.

Barca president Joan Laporta has also been vocal about his determination to sign Alvarez.

Chelsea and City are for now not speaking publicly about the Fernandez situation.

But their positions are clear.

The London club insist they have played fair by Fernandez and City.

Informed by the player’s entourage of his desire to leave, in late May the Blues set out the terms under which they would be prepared for it to happen.

Namely: a formal written offer of a guaranteed fee of £120m payable, it is understood, in three chunky instalments, rather than slightly smaller sums spread over a longer period. With those terms available only until 5pm last Friday.

Very few clubs in the world are capable of spending so much on one player. Real Madrid are one, but their interest faded and – for now at least – has not reawakened.



City are another. But they are adamant they will not splash £120m for Fernandez.

The imminent sale of Rodri makes no difference. City will have known before the weekend they were on course to agree a deal with Barcelona for the Spain midfielder.

Yet they still let the Friday deadline pass without making a formal bid for Fernandez.

Money is not the issue, although City are set to spend all of the £65.4m Rodri fee and more on Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Etihad bosses have made it known they will not pay £120m.

Chelsea chiefs say they will not accept anything less and, in any case, that exit package for Fernandez is no longer available.

Which is why the Blues say they now expect the 25 year old to stay at the club this season.

But with the transfer window still open, the story has a fortnight, at least, still to run.



It is worth stepping back and asking why City and Maresca want Fernandez.

As Chelsea themselves noted in May ahead of the last game of the season, only five Premier League players have registered more than the Argentinian’s 48 goal contributions – 24 goals and 24 assists – since the start of the 2024/5 campaign.

Fernandez was playing under Maresca for about three quarters of that period and is understood to credit the Italian with helping him to be more decisive in the opposition half.

City are in a process of transition, with the departure of Guardiola and a number of players.

Rodri has now followed Bernardo Silva to Barcelona, leaving huge midfield holes for the club to fill.

Elliot Anderson and Bouaddi, either together or one at a time, will perform some of Rodri and Silva’s jobs.

But City also need a midfielder who can make runs from deep to create and score goals, after Tijjani Reijnders was allowed to leave following just one season at the club.

If you look in detail at the data, it becomes clear Fernandez is one of the best at doing it in the world.



Add into the equation the Argentinian’s all-round attributes and competitive edge, and the question becomes: why would Chelsea even consider letting him go?

It is interesting to note that one of the players ahead of Fernandez in the PL chart of goal contributions was Morgan Rogers, whom the Blues signed in a £117m deal which is a record for a British player.

Rogers made a promising debut in the 3-1 friendly win over Real Sociedad at the weekend. You would expect any decent player to put away the rebound from which he scored the opener.

But the England star’s movement and understanding with two-goal Joao Pedro were impressive.

Although Fernandez has played in an advanced and/or more free role for Chelsea and Argentina, Rogers is more suited to playing as one of the No 10s that new Blues manager Xabi Alonso uses in his favoured 4-2-3-1 formation.

In short: Chelsea aim to be less reliant on the kind of attacking attributes which are Fernandez’s speciality.

Then there is the issue of the Blues fans booing the guy who is still nominally their vice captain.

You could expect the ill feeling which comes from his behaviour in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final win over England to die down as the season goes on. Among Chelsea supporters in any case, and many of them did sing Fernandez’s name.



But Alonso will want to avoid anything poisoning the feelgood factor he has been building.

The word is the Chelsea camp has been a happy place to be over the summer. Alonso’s achievements at Bayer Leverkusen and, more significantly, his stellar career as a player, ensured he received immediate respect.

Unlike poor predecessor Liam Rosenior, who was fighting fires from the moment he arrived.

Rosenior was further undermined by Fernandez and Marc Cucurella talking out of turn.

Cucurella was sold to Atletico Madrid before the World Cup. Alejandro Garnacho, another player with the potential to cause unrest, has left on loan.

But Fernandez is back after his extended break following the tournament and the danger is his presence will sour the atmosphere.

Finally, there is the issue of money.

Chelsea have plenty of other players they need to find new homes for in the next couple of weeks. They were very successful sellers last summer and will be confident of repeating the trick.



But a big fee for Fernandez, a player they rate highly but could survive without, would be a welcome boost to their coffers.

The Blues still have to meet the strict terms on losses laid down in their settlement with Uefa for breaking financial rules, despite not playing in European competition this season.

Although Fernandez was signed for £106m rising to £110m in January 2023, his value on the Chelsea books is now somewhere between £65m and £70m.

That is because of the accounting process of amortisation, which reduces the value of a player as an intangible asset over the course of their contract. So a £100m fee would represent a good profit.

Yet the Blues can legitimately argue Fernandez is a better player than the one they signed three and a half years ago. And therefore worth every penny of £120m or more, especially in a market inflated by deals like the £116m City have paid for Anderson.

Chelsea know all the reasons why City want to sign Fernandez as well.

But City also know all the reasons why Chelsea would be prepared to sell him.

Football, and the transfer market in particular, teaches you to be cynical.

Clubs can swear blind they will not be buying or selling a particular player, only for a deal to be done in the end.

Whatever anyone says, whether in public or through briefings, is really just a position from which to negotiate. Nothing is set in stone.



But when a player is of the quality and status of Fernandez, the stakes are higher.

Chelsea will look silly if they sell him for less than £120m. And Blues bosses have turned down numerous offers to sponsor their shirts under the current regime, refusing to budge in their valuation. Even if it looks self-defeating from the outside.

They could keep a world-class footballer at the club, hope the hostility dies down, and wait to cash in on him later. Any sale before June 30 next year would still count for this season’s financial results.

City will appear desperate if they agree to pay £120m for Fernandez after saying there was no chance they would. They could look at other targets or go with what they have.

Although that will be harder if they do not improve on their Community Shield performance in the early games of the new season.

Finding a deal this summer which everyone can present as a success will be hard.

Which is why the Fernandez saga may well run until close to 11pm on September 1, when the window closes.

And not be resolved even then.

Sports.title: Fifa chief SACKED by Gianni Infantino weeks after blasting shameless World Cup sell-off plot
Sports.content:
THE first Fifa chief to bravely blast Gianni Infantino’s World Cup selling scheme has been sacked.

Kevin Lamour was the world football governing body’s chief operating officer.



However, he put his neck out to slam the money-grabbing plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments to raise £20billion.

Lamour, 46, insisted Infantino acted alone and was willing to lose his job over his bold comments.



And so it has proved as Fifa confirmed his departure.

As reported by The Times, a spokesperson said: “The working relationship between Fifa and Kevin Lamour as Fifa’s chief operating officer has ended.



“Fifa thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future.

“No further comment will be made on the matter.”

Secretary general Mattias Grafstrom shared the news with Fifa employees via email.

In a separate email to the top brass of the organisation, Grafstrom added: “Following recent discussions, Fifa and our chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, have agreed to part ways.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally.

“Kevin joined Fifa in November 2024 and in this time has overseen a period of significant change, including improved relationships with stakeholders and the delivery of several significant projects of joint interest, amongst many other key achievements.

“I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of Fifa on a daily basis.”

Lamour launched his stinging statement in response to the Infantino project on July 31.



He said: “To put it very clearly and directly: the project that has sparked so much controversy and debate is not a Fifa project. It is even less a project of Fifa’s administration. It is the project of one person.

“The Fifa vice-presidents, the members of the Fifa Council, the confederations, the federations, the players, the leagues, the clubs, and the fans were not the only ones who were ignored.

“Fifa’s own administration was also deceived. This lie by omission over many months and this unilateral exercise of power are not trivial.

“They are indicative of a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance. And a serious lack of respect.

“Not only must this project not go ahead — for obvious reasons that need not even be listed here — but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.



“Regarding this project and what comes next. Everyone must take responsibility. Because it is becoming increasingly difficult for Fifa’s administration to work under these conditions and fulfil its mission.

“My feeling is that we all want to be proud to work for Fifa, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us. That saddens me.

“My colleagues — some of whom have dedicated their lives to football — deserve better than contempt and intimidation.

“The ball is now in the court of those who have the power to change things. I know I have a duty of loyalty to my employer.

“But I also, and above all, have a duty of loyalty to certain values and to the upbringing I have received, and a duty to support my colleagues.



“And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

The other significant departure from Fifa since the news broke of the controversial plans was Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino’s senior advisor.

However, Swiss top dog Infantino is still clinging on to his role as Fifa president despite the widespread backlash.

A damning open letter from Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC last week saw him accused of “breaking trust through deception”.

SunSport understands Concacaf, Uefa and the AFC are pressurising Infantino to resign with immediate effect and not run for re-election for a fourth term in March.



LaLiga chief Javier Tebas, meanwhile, insisted the Infantino era is “over” and he is “destroying the very essence of football”.

But as well as the scandalous attempt to privatise the World Cup, it has also been revealed in bombshell documents that Infantino was actually plotting to partner with the rebel breakaway European Super League – and it could even have been called the Fifa Super League.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Also, The Telegraph reported that Uefa paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of married Infantino while he was general secretary.

And SunSport revealed his latest blow that even his hometown club Zug 94 in Switzerland are refusing to back his beleaguered leadership.

Sports.title: FA must end the Tonda Eckert saga with Saints boss facing up to a six-month ban
Sports.content:
FA bigwigs need to stop faffing about — and bring an end to the Tonda Eckert spygate saga.

It has been almost THREE MONTHS since the EFL threw Southampton out of the play-off final against Middlesbrough while slapping them with a four-point deduction this season.



Yet the new campaign kicked off this weekend with the Saints boss still awaiting the outcome of an additional FA investigation.

And the German could face a potential touchline ban of six months.



Eckert responded to the new charge of bringing the game into disrepute weeks ago — travelling to London to answer questions directly from disciplinary officials.

So why on earth are the FA still dragging this process out?



The EFL disciplinary commission took 11 days from initially charging Southampton for snooping on a Middlesbrough training session to meting out the unprecedented punishment.

You have to wonder why it took TWO MONTHS for the FA to even decide to throw the book at Eckert in the first place?

Surely once Southampton were expelled from the play-offs, the dark suits at Wembley should have charged him within days if they felt there was a case to answer.

Call me cynical — but is it because some of them were on a jolly at the World Cup with England instead?



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It does seem interesting the charge only landed a couple of days after the Three Lions returned from the tournament with all the hangers-on.

What Eckert and Southampton did was wrong. It goes against integrity and fair play.

But I’m afraid that word left football a long time ago.

There is reasonable mitigation to what Eckert did, which although does not exonerate him does at least explain his actions — however unpalatable.



When Will Still was appointed Southampton manager last summer, he was given a full, official breakdown of EFL and FA regulations.

But when Eckert was promoted from his role as under-21s head coach following Still’s sacking in November, nobody at the club or governing body sat the German down to explain the finer points of EFL rules.

That was an administrative howler from the club.

The Middlesbrough incident didn’t start as some elaborate military operation. It began with the analysis team idly discussing whether Hayden Hackney was fit to play in a staff meeting.

When someone pointed out Boro’s training ground was right next to a public golf course, a decision was made to send young intern Will Salt over to have a look.



Having spent years coaching in Germany and Italy, where observing an opponent’s open-air sessions is standard practice, Eckert claims he did not realise the EFL had unique restrictions.

I accept that. There’s not another league in European football that has such a rule.

Even here, in the Premier League, National League and non-league, there is no regulation restricting it.

The FA themselves do not spell out that observing another team ahead of a game is prohibited.

EFL bigwigs only wrote it into their rules when Leeds were caught snooping on Derby in 2019.



The FA did not charge Leeds or their then manager Marcelo Bielsa after the EFL hit the club with a fine for breaking “good faith” regulations.

Yes, the EFL rules changed — but the FA’s didn’t.

So what makes this case different?

Eckert has been found guilty of spying on three clubs — Middlesbrough, Ipswich and Oxford — as opposed to ex-Leeds boss Marcelo Bielsa admitting he spied on EVERY opponent!

Once the Argentine gave his epic briefing to the media showing how he did it, there was an acceptance that this was a coach who simply did not understand English football culture. In fact, most people found it entertaining rather than being outraged.



And because he was not even punished — although he paid the £200,000 fine the club received out of his own pocket — it did not seem a big deal — especially on the continent.

Then there is putting things into perspective.

Chelsea admitted 74 breaches of FA agents rules — and were only slapped recently with a £10m fine, minor by Premier League standards. Not even a single point was docked — and no ban from being involved in the game from any of the parties responsible.

Eckert has spent the summer making sure he understands all the rules and has accepted what he did was wrong.

The punishment of stopping what could have been promotion to the Premier League was massive. The points deduction added further salt into those wounds.



It is time to move on and let the young coach get on with his career — and Southampton to focus on getting back to where they belong.

Who didn’t eat all the pies?

WHO ate all the pies — or, in the hospitality boxes at Wolves on Friday, who didn’t?

The club put on some lovely steak & ale offerings — and vegetarian options — during their Championship opener against Blackburn.

Yet I was aghast to see several trolleys with trays almost full of uneaten pies in the corridors at Molineux.

One of the guilty parties was the box belonging to returning Molineux hero Raul Jimenez.



So it was a case of ‘No, senor.”

Perhaps the Wolves fans should reword the lyrics of their famous song to .. “Our Number 9 … pass him a pie and he’ll leave it behind!”

Back where they belong …

BURNLEY punters at The Turf next to the stadium appeared to have accepted Premier League exit in the good spirit.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prior to their Championship opener with fellow relegated club West Ham, a flag was flying proudly above the entrance, which read: “Burnley, No Nay Never … Back where we belong!”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick can finally bury the ghost and do something no Man Utd manager has done since Sir Alex Ferguson
Sports.content:
FOR Michael Carrick and Manchester United, it is time to bury the ghost.

Maybe not to win the Premier League title again this season — that might prove too much of a stretch. But to end 13 years of being second best in their own city.



What is incredible — given United’s domination of the first two decades of the Prem — is that Carrick, 45, was a key member of the last Red Devils side to finish ahead of Manchester City.

As shock recruit Robin van Persie starred to give Sir Alex Ferguson his perfect farewell — regaining the crown ripped from his grasp by Sergio Aguero’s unforgettable intervention with the final goal of the previous campaign — United fans were prepared for a testing time.



They won that 2013 title with four games to spare, finishing 11 points clear of City, but looked like a side running their final race.

Change is often complicated. Time is the ultimate enemy of every football career. Nothing is set in stone.



When you lose the greatest manager, whose reign was an iron rod of relentless focus, there was always going to be a reckoning.

Nobody could have imagined that it would see the beginning of an era of City being the top dogs — by a distance the standout side who were to bag an astonishing 19 major trophies, including seven Prem titles.

United have tried to match them, opting for the “Chosen One” in David Moyes — in fact, it was a hospital pass for the Scot — then a host of big names, a couple of up-and- comers from abroad and, in various caretaker and full-time roles, five Old Trafford “legends”.

Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho were serial winners — course AND distance in the case of the “Special One”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim were seen as the next generation; Ralf Rangnick a human bridging loan who was prepared to spell out some uncomfortable truths.

The United knowledge of Ryan Giggs, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick himself, Ruud van Nistelrooy and Darren Fletcher . . . none of them were able to do anything to close the gap, which became a chasm as Pep Guardiola took City to the commanding heights.

But Guardiola is now gone. It is City who have to undergo the painful transition — the scale of which suddenly appeared more significant in Cardiff on Sunday.

Of course, United manager Carrick has to answer the doubts, perhaps some within his own mind.

Solskjaer, he will know, looked to have cracked it in his caretaker spell. Taking the reins full-time proved a far more challenging task, one that was beyond the Norwegian.



Yet Carrick will be able to point to a settled approach — and one that has worked. Dispensing with Amorim’s flailing, failing back three, reverting to a system that suited the players at his disposal, Carrick got United to look like . . . well, like United.

After the Geordie took charge with 17 games to go last term, the Red Devils picked up 39 points – more than any other side.

That was three points ahead of champions Arsenal, while City earned 35 and Liverpool just 25.

Translating that into a full campaign, when Carrick is responsible for anything that goes wrong rather than solely taking credit for the positives, is a different proposition.

United need to sort out the left-back issue, require an extra midfield body and must manage the demands of the Champions League.



At the same time, the physical and emotional toll of the varying World Cup experiences of Senne Lammens, Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes, Mateus Cunha and the potentially reintegrated Marcus Rashford will be new situations with which Carrick must juggle.

The transfer splurge craved by supporters has not materialised.

However, the captures of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, Rashford’s likely return to arms and retaining their attacking armoury — Fernandes, Cunha, Bryan Mbuemo and Benjamin Sesko scored 41 Premier League goals between them — give United a platform.

The Old Trafford faithful, of course, crave a return to the summit. But ending that long wait to finish above City again would be a significant step. For United and Carrick.

Potential balls-up

I FEEL Premier League chiefs missed a trick not using the World Cup-style “connected ball” this season.



Spain’s LaLiga, which also uses Puma footballs, kicked off last weekend with a chip in the match ball after linking up with Fifa’s partner Kinexon.

But Prem chiefs are sticking with the same VAR set-up as last term, arguing that the extra cameras used for their semi-automated offside technology renders the chip redundant.

It means that VARs will have to make calls on potential handballs by goalscorers, or faint touches that could determine offsides, based on incomplete evidence.

Benjamin Sesko’s goal in Manchester United’s win over Liverpool last season was an example of a situation where the connected ball would have brought a conclusive verdict.

Surely the best league in the world should use the best available kit.



Bringing sexy track

THE GOLDEN girls shone bright in Birmingham, with Amy Hunt leading the way at the European Championships.

After too long in which British athletes seemed to have been ordered to be automatons when facing the media, Hunt, Georgia Hunter Bell, plus silver-winning Keely Hodgkinson, were among those whose honesty and willingness to engage was refreshing.

Full houses for the last few days have boosted London’s claims to host the 2029 Worlds. Track and field is sexy again.

Feels like a turning point

MANCHESTER CITY fans who made the trip to Cardiff did not need a government text alert to see the warning signs facing Enzo Maresca’s side.

Yet the sight of them turning their backs on the Community Shield was satisfying for Arsenal fans. A pre-season game means nothing in itself. But it could be a signpost.



Parachutes fail to open

SO much for a predictable Championship campaign — with none of the four “parachute” clubs winning their openers.

Burnley, West Ham and Wolves all drew — admittedly two of them met at Turf Moor — while Southampton, still seemingly affected by Spygate repercussions, lost at Watford.

Over the next nine months, the quartet do have a big advantage. But they have to earn it on the pitch. Ask Leicester.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Step in the right direction

CREDIT to Bournemouth for admitting they fumbled in their clumsy dismissals of long-standing match-day staff.

It may not ease the anger of those let go, but conceding that employees “deserve to be treated with respect” and this “did not reflect the standards we expect of ourselves as a club” was a step in the right direction.

Sports.title: Conor Gallagher to become a dad as Tottenham star and model fiancee Aine May announce pregnancy
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM star Conor Gallagher is set to become a dad for the first time.

The 26-year-old and his fiancee, Aine May Kennedy, announced they are expecting their first child with a heartwarming Instagram post.



Aine May posted six photos of them in a field with three scan images.

Their dog was also in the announcement pictures.



The post was captioned: “Our greatest adventure is about to begin. Baby Gallagher, January 2027.”

Gallagher and Aine May swiftly received messages from friends and followers, with Tottenham striker Mikey Moore writing: “Congratulations,” with two blue hearts.

Britney De Villiers, Morgan Gibbs-White‘s fiancee, said: “Congratulations!”

Megan Pickford, Jordan Pickford‘s wife, added: “Congratulations beautiful lady!”

While Kate Kane, Harry Kane‘s wife, also wrote: “Congratulations!”

Gallagher and Aine May began dating in 2020 and got engaged while on a romantic holiday to Mallorca in June.



The midfielder is currently preparing for his first full season at Tottenham, having moved to the London club in January from Atletico Madrid.

He told Sky Sports last week: “It’s time to kick on to try and show the fans what I can do.

“I want to be at my best to help the club go to where we should be.



“Every footballer has things going on and hard, tough times. It’s just life. Everyone has problems and I’m just really happy that we came out of it and I ended the season well.

“Hopefully this is only the start of my Spurs career.”

Sports.title: Four players Arsenal could sell before window closes after Mikel Arteta complaints
Sports.content:
Four players Arsenal could sell before window closes after Mikel Arteta complaints

Arsenal are running out of time to sell unwanted players in the summer transfer window and Mikel Arteta voiced his frustrations following their Community Shield win on Sunday

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal have too many players for a matchday squad (Image: Ryan Pierse/The FA via Getty Images)

Arsenal are looking to offload four fringe players who failed to make the squad for their Community Shield win over Manchester City on Sunday. The Gunners kicked off their campaign by thrashing their Premier League title rivals 3-0, with Mikel Arteta's squad giving a hint at potential transfer exits.

‌



While all eyes were on new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis, who made their competitive debuts in Cardiff, Arteta's squad said plenty about those not included. Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Ethan Nwaneri, Marli Salmon, Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson were all missing from the matchday squad.

‌



Martinelli is the subject of interest from Galatasaray who have tabled a bid worth €45million (£38m) for the striker, who is reportedly not keen on moving to Turkey. The Brazilian forward has entered the final year of his contract, but appears likely to stay put unless a different transfer proposal emerges.

‌



Salmon is a 16-year-old defender who has made four first-team appearances for Arsenal, but will have to remain patient for further opportunities. The other four players who were uninvolved at the weekend could be sold before the September 1 transfer deadline.

‌



The Athletic reports that Vieira and Nelson are the subject of interest from Hamburg and West Ham respectively after spending last season away on loan. Meanwhile, Napoli are keen to sign Jesus, who is in the final 12 months of his deal, and the Gunners could reluctantly part company with Nwaneri too.

Nwaneri faces a challenge to get minutes in Arsenal's stacked midfield and there is a grudging realisation that a transfer may be the best outcome, especially as the homegrown player would count as pure profit on the balance sheet. The 19-year-old spent last season on loan with Marseille and AC Milan and Galatasaray are among the clubs to formally make enquiries this summer.

The competition for places at Arsenal has led to the club needing to offload fringe players, with Arteta frustrated that he can't include more players on the substitutes' bench.

‌



View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri was in Cardiff on Sunday but didn't make the squad (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

“It’s really sad not to have their availability," Arteta told TNT Sports after the win. "I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend and accommodate more players in the squad because they deserve to be in the squad, there’s no question.

“Ethan and Marli as well, who has had the whole pre-season with us. Hopefully we can change that rule so players can enjoy on the pitch and can be an option to play and contribute to the team going forward.”

‌



Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta is working hard to try and agree some sales, with Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) the only players have left the club for transfer fees this summer.

Sales are needed to help fund incoming deals for a central defender to provide cover for the injured William Saliba and world-class attacker.

Sports.title: Sky Sports ditch Baller League despite strong viewing figures and Premier League claim
Sports.content:
Sky Sports ditch Baller League despite strong viewing figures and Premier League claim

Baller League, a six-a-side tournament aimed at younger audiences, is heading into its fourth season, but it will no longer be broadcast by Sky Sports

View 2 Images Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge are among those involved in Baller League (Image: Baller League)

Baller League will no longer be shown on Sky Sports after the broadcaster decided to drop the six-a-side tournament. The influencer-packed competition has been given a platform by Sky, but its upcoming fourth season will be shown on YouTube instead.

‌



Baller League has involvement from content creators like KSI and AngryGinge, as well as ex-players and media personalities like Micah Richards, Ian Wright, Alan Shearer and Daniel Sturridge and current star Chloe Kelly. With celebrities, including actor Idris Elba, as team managers and some recognisable faces playing, it has proven to be a hit with younger audiences.

‌



However, The Guardian reports that Sky have decided not to renew their contract for the next season, despite being happy with viewing figures and social media engagement. Baller League will therefore go free-to-air, broadcasting the fourth season on YouTube. Mirror Football has contacted Baller League to request comment.

‌



While it appears to be a significant setback for Baller League, the company's chief executive Felix Starck has big plans for the future. "I still think that we're going to see Premier League teams in Baller League sooner rather than later," he told Sky Sports in May.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"We have a lot of things that teams are missing. One thing is the future generation [who are] consuming us and they have a lot that we are missing, which is established scouting systems, training grounds, history, culture and networks.

‌



"So they certainly have more that we are missing but we have one big thing that they're missing, that they're all worried about, which is 'who is going to watch me in 15 years?'.

"If you have a six-a-side team as Arsenal, Chelsea, Man City or Man United... you let your 16 or 17-year-olds go because they're physically under-developed - why not stick them in your six-a-side team? Why not grow fans there and build a bridge to the 11-a-side team?"

View 2 Images Stephen Ireland and Henri Lansbury playing for Deportrio in the Baller League (Image: Baller League)

‌



Baller League matches consist of two 15-minute halves, with teams able to influence the game further through 'Gamechanger' moments in the final three minutes of each half. These include long-range goals counting double or the six-on-six format changing to three-on-three.

Former Manchester City defender and current pundit Richards is in charge of a team called Deportrio. He has embraced the Baller League ethos and is certain it will continue to go from strength to strength.

"It's a better standard than people think," Richards told Mirror Football in November. "People are watching at home and thinking, it's just like a small little tournament. But if you're not fit then you get found out straight away.

Article continues below

"Especially in the first season, everyone was... saying 'what is this?' and now everyone absolutely loves it. If you look at my inbox and my Instagram, probably, I wouldn't say thousands, but hundreds of people wanting to play. That's how big it's become."

Sports.title: Sheffield United facing 'real prospect' of 12-point deduction in battle with ex-owner
Sports.content:
Sheffield United facing 'real prospect' of 12-point deduction in battle with ex-owner

Sheffield United's former owner Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is pursuing current owners Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen in court over alleged unpaid millions

View 2 Images Sheffield United's ex-owner Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is behind the claims (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

Sheffield United's former owner claims the Championship club could be facing a 12-point deduction due to a row over money with the current owners.

‌



Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud sold the Blades to Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen for just over £100million in December 2024. But now Prince Adbullah's company, United World, is attempting to wind up the company which bought the club.

‌



It is claimed that COH Sports Bidco Ltd (CSBL) still owes £35m in missing installments for the purchase of the club. A hearing has been set at a London court on Wednesday.

‌



"In short, they are trying to take the club without paying for it," United World said in a statement on Monday. In response, a spokesperson for the ownership group of Eltoukhy and Rosen described the petition as "a publicity stunt" and claimed the club is more “financially healthy” now than under his ownership.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

They also said they had invited the prince to “reinvest in the club and join the ownership of Sheffield United” again, adding that the co-owners “are focused on the sustainability of the club and the season ahead”.

‌



The dispute centres around the decision to transfer Sheffield United’s shares from previous parent company CSBL to another one called 1919 Partners earlier this summer. Prince Abdullah claims that is an attempt to "avoid paying CSBL’s creditors".

United World said in a statement: "If the winding-up petition is granted on 19 August, as we expect, EFL Regulation 2.1.16 provides that Rosen must be disqualified from being a controlling owner and director of SUFC.

View 2 Images Sheffield United's current and former owner are in a financial dispute (Image: Maynard Manyowa/Getty Images)

‌



"He will no longer be able to be chairman, or a director, he will no longer be able to exercise any control over the club and will have to sell a significant proportion of his controlling interest in the club.

"In addition, we understand that, once investigations are completed, there is a real prospect that the EFL may have to impose a 12-point deduction on SUFC under EFL Regulation 12.3, in order to 'protect the integrity and continuity of the League Competition' and 'the reputation of The League'."

United World have hired leading sports lawyer Nick De Marco and added: “As the former owners of SUFC, United World does not want to see SUFC facing months of uncertainty that will follow the winding-up order being granted on 19 August, but in the absence of Eltoukhy and Rosen, both billionaires, agreeing to pay what they owe, we have no alternative but to take all legal steps to protect our interests."

Article continues below

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire told BBC Radio Sheffield: "I think that (a winding up) is the worse-case scenario. Clearly United World are serious in the sense that they are entitled to be paid and the instalments that were due, there's no justification in those being missed by the new owners of Sheffield United."

"I've seen a lot of winding up orders relating to football clubs over the years. The vast majority are either settled on the court room steps before it goes into court, or the defending team will ask for some sort of postponement. I think it's unlikely that the company will be wound up on Wednesday."

Sports.title: Arsenal could offer Brighton five players to beat Man Utd to statement signing
Sports.content:
Arsenal could offer Brighton five players to beat Man Utd to statement signing

Arsenal are continuing their business in the summer transfer window ahead of the Premier League season beginning

View 6 Images Mikel Arteta could offload a number of players to land the Brighton midfielder (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal could offer five players to Brighton to land Jack Hinshelwood. Mikel Arteta still aims to add to his squad after spending around £144million so far this summer.

‌



The Gunners boss plans to bring in more transfers ahead of their Premier League opener against Coventry City. Hinshelwood is one of Arsenal's primary targets and the club could consider swap deals to facilitate the move.

‌



Club officials have reportedly contacted the midfielder's representatives, with an official bid ready to be made. However, Manchester United are also keen on Hinshelwood so Arsenal may need to make their offer more attractive to Brighton.

‌



Player swaps have become something of a trend this summer following Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson's switch between Everton and Crystal Palace. McNeil headed south to join the Eagles while Johnson arrived on Merseyside to work under David Moyes.

Mikel Arteta 'fighting' to change Premier League rule that would suit Arsenal READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta sends clear transfer message to three Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield READ MORE :

The Gunners may take inspiration from this deal and offer Brighton some of their own squad to land Hinshelwood. Here, Mirror Football has looked at who Arsenal could put forward in a swap deal with the Seagulls to reduce the £51m asking price.

Gabriel Jesus

Gabriel Jesus is one of the most likely options given Brighton's desire for a centre-forward and Arsenal's openness to letting him go. The Brazilian was omitted from the Gunners' Community Shield squad at the weekend and has been heavily linked with a move.

‌



View 6 Images Gabriel Jesus could be the next departure for Arteta (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Serie A side Napoli have registered an interest with Arsenal keen to get rid of Jesus' £265,000-a-week wages. Brighton are in the market for a striker following Danny Welbeck's move to Chelsea and could consider the 29-year-old.

Myles Lewis-Skelly

Myles Lewis-Skelly was a standout performer in Sunday's 3-0 win over Manchester City, assisting Riccardo Calafiori's superb strike in the 23rd second. The versatile star has been heavily involved throughout Arsenal's pre-season tour but has been linked with a move away from north London.

‌



View 6 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly has been touted with an exit (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The England international was offered to Chelsea and Manchester United earlier this window. If Arsenal still want him off the books then he could be used in a deal with Brighton.

Lewis-Skelly's potential is still sky high, given his youth, and the 19-year-old can play across the middle of the park as well as both full-back positions.

‌



Ethan Nwaneri

View 6 Images Ethan Nwaneri is likely to depart north London this summer (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Ethan Nwaneri's departure remains likely this summer after ending up on loan to Marseille last season. The 19-year-old is under contract until 2030 and the Gunners may be leaning more towards another temporary move.

Martin Zubimendi has shone for Arsenal since joining from Real Sociedad last summer. The Spaniard won the Premier League title at the first time of asking and Real Madrid have already expressed interest.

With Bruno Guimaraes joining earlier this month for £75m, Zubimendi may see his game time dwindling and could opt to move elsewhere to continue his upward trajectory.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Bruno Fernandes bid incoming as Marcus Rashford to Barcelona still on
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Bruno Fernandes bid incoming as Marcus Rashford to Barcelona still on

Manchester United's Premier League season begins away at Hull City but there could still be some transfers completed before their opener

View 3 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has just four days until the new Premier League season begins (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have four days until their Premier League opener against Hull City. But Michael Carrick's squad has only been bolstered by three new arrivals thus far.

‌



In what has been Carrick's first pre-season at the helm, United have fared reasonably, winning two, losing two and drawing two. Their final friendly was against AC Milan and ex-manager Ruben Amorim, when they fell to a 4-2 defeat in Poland.

‌



Over the summer window, three senior additions have been made. Andrey Santos was signed from Chelsea for £50m, Karl Darlow joined after his Leeds United deal expired and Youri Tielemans arrived from Aston Villa for £35m.

‌



However, with less than two weeks left until the window shuts, major speculation surrounding Bruno Fernandes and Marcus Rashford is rife. Mirror Football brings you the latest out of Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd issue instant response to shock Bruno Fernandes transfer approach READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher says Man Utd won't win the title and names player they should have signed READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford U-turn

Rashford's future has been a topic of conversation throughout this summer transfer window after the English forward returned to United following a loan spell at Barcelona.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and scored 14 goals (Image: Getty)

The 28-year-old played well in La Liga, but the Catalan giants opted not to make his loan move permanent for £26m, instead opting to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle for £70m and Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

Rashford was left in limbo, with suggestions that he might be fully reintegrated at Old Trafford for the new season. However, new reports claim that Barcelona are not quite done.

‌



TEAMtalk claims they remain in contact with Rashford's representatives and despite making a series of attacking signings, continue to assess their options and could still attempt to pull off a dramatic return.

Rashford returned to United training on August 9 after starring for England at the World Cup. He played in their 4-2 defeat to AC Milan.

‌



Bruno Fernandes bid

In another shock revelation, United are braced for Galatasaray to mount a bid for captain Fernandes. In May, Mirror Football reported that the Portuguese playmaker would be a dream signing for the Turkish side.

Now, it appears they are doing all they can to entice him to Istanbul, with The Telegraph claiming they are ready to double his wages and offer £43m for Fernandes' services.

View 3 Images Fernandes has been linked with a move to Turkey (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

However, multiple outlets have suggested that United will swiftly reject the offer and any future bid, as they consider their skipper completely untouchable. His £55.6m release clause for foreign clubs expired in July.

BBC Sport specifically claims that Galatasaray would be wasting their time and that they are not the only club that might attempt to test United's resolve. Both Juventus and AC Milan have been suggested as potential interested parties. Fernandes' current contract expires in 2027, with the option to extend it by a further year.

Sports.title: Man Utd holding Bruno Fernandes future talks after big money offer received
Sports.content:
Man Utd holding Bruno Fernandes future talks after big money offer received

Bruno Fernandes is in the final year of his Manchester United contract, albeit the club still have an option to extend their captain's deal by another 12 months

View 2 Images Manchester United are adamant that they want to keep Bruno Fernandes this summer (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester United are said to be engaged in contract discussions with Bruno Fernandes. It follows reports that Galatasaray have made a £17million proposal to their club captain.

‌



Fernandes, 31, last put pen to paper on fresh terms two years ago this month, which featured a £56million release clause for foreign clubs, though that clause lapsed earlier in this summer transfer window. His existing deal is set to run until the end of this season, with a one-year option.

‌



However, the Portugal international apparently wants to stay at United The Athletic reports that they are adamant that no clubs have made contact.

‌



Man Utd issue instant response to shock Bruno Fernandes transfer approach READ MORE :

Man Utd left red-faced as MUTV coverage of AC Milan clash cuts out READ MORE :

Al-Hilal have previously made overtures to Fernandes, who rejected the Saudi Pro League side last year. He said late last year of that interest: "I could have left as many people do and said: 'I want to leave, I don't want to train, I just want to leave for €20million or €30million, so they pay me more on the other side', but I never did that."

"I never felt in a position to do that, because I felt that the empathy and affection I had for the club were the same. But there comes a point where, for them, money is more important than anything.

"The club wanted me to go; I have that in my head. I told the directors this, but I think they didn't have the courage to make that decision.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has suggested publicly that he wants to stay at Manchester United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

"I decided to stay, also because of family reasons, but because I genuinely like the club. "The conversation with the manager also made me stay.

"But, from the club's side, I felt a bit like, 'If you leave, it's not so bad for us'. It hurts me a lot.

‌



"More than hurting, it makes me sad because I'm a player they have nothing to criticise about. I'm always available, and I always play - good or bad - I give my all. Then you see things around you, players who don't value the club as much and don't defend the club as much... that makes you sad."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Fernandes remarked earlier this summer: "Playing for Manchester United is always a special moment for everyone. At the same time, it brings a lot of responsibility with it.

‌



"But I don't think anyone comes to Manchester United thinking that we won't have the responsibility to win again, to be at the top of Premier League, at the top of European football.

"Because the club's history brings that responsibility. Regardless of the most recent years they were not at the level that the club was used to.

"I think everyone always believes that we can be the ones who are going to do this, the ones who are going to turn the page, the ones who are going to make it possible for United to fight on all fronts.

Article continues below

"And I think that has to be special for us players, to realise that we can be the main, let's say, protagonists of this change of history for United to win again."

Liverpool reach agreement with PSG star as attacking double deal takes shape

Liverpool are making progress in their efforts to sign Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye this summer, with an agreement reached with one of the PSG talents

View Image Liverpool have reached an agreement for Ibrahim Mbaye (Image: Al Bello, Getty Images)

Liverpool have reached an agreement with Ibrahim Mbaye as they look to snap up the forward and his Paris Saint-Germain team-mate, Bradley Barcola. It's been a largely quiet transfer window for the Reds, as Andoni Iraola looks to make a difference in 2026/27.

‌



Mohamed Salah, Ibrahima Konate and Andy Robertson have each left the club as free agents, with Liverpool bringing in Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo as replacements. ‌



Barcola has been linked with a move to Merseyside for the duration of the summer. PSG, meanwhile, are reluctant to let the 23-year-old winger leave, initially slapping a price tag of around £145million on him to deter any potential suitors.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president

FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, said that he and his colleagues had been 'deceived' by Gianni Infantino's now scrapped plan to sell the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino continues to receive backlash (Image: Jared C. Tilton - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA has sacked its chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, after he criticised president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off the World Cup. Lamour, a longtime colleague of Infantino at both FIFA and UEFA, said that staff had been 'deceived' by the plan which has now been scrapped following widespread backlash.

‌



Sky News first reported Lamour's departure. While FIFA chose not to comment on the nature of his exit, football's world governing body did offer a statement.

‌



"FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA's Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026," the statement read. "FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future."

‌



A letter sent by FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom has also surfaced. It informed FIFA staff about Lamour's departure, with the Frenchman having been with the organisation since November 2024.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Following recent discussions, FIFA and our Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour have agreed to part ways," Grafstrom said. "This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally.

"Kevin joined FIFA in November 2024 and in this time has overseen a period of significant change, including improved relationships with stakeholders and the delivery of several significant projects of joint interest, amongst many other key achievements.

"You will have seen Kevin present in each FIFA Council meeting since his appointment in 2024, and many of you will have had a regular working relationship with Kevin on projects of various kinds since his joining FIFA.

‌



Is Gianni Infantino's position untenable? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Kevin Lamour was with FIFA for nearly two years (Image: Joosep Martinson - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

"I felt it was important that I personally provide you this update and I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of FIFA on a daily basis. I wish Kevin all the best for the future." Last month, Lamour made headlines by saying that he and his colleagues were 'deceived' by Infantino's plan to sell FIFA competitions, including the men's World Cup to private investors, labelling it 'the project of one person'. The 45-year-old also suggested that the under-fire president should step down from the position which he's held since 2016.

Article continues below

"Not only must this project not go ahead," Lamour wrote. "But the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions."

Sports.title: England begin new Test cricket era with old captain and no Stokes
Sports.content:
Who's ready for another reset?

England had one of those after their dismal Ashes winter and it started well enough with a Lord's victory over New Zealand, albeit in a two-day rollercoaster ride on a dreadful pitch that meant it was hard to gauge whether any genuine progress had been made.

But that reset soon came crashing down amid familiar old failings of drink-related off-field incidents and witless shots on it. A depleted England side were annihilated at The Oval before a drubbing at Trent Bridge consigned them to a rare home Test series loss.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes took a wicket against New Zealand moments after announcing his retirement from international cricket on day four of the third Test at Trent Bridge in June

Captain Ben Stokes decided he had had enough (bizarrely revealing that midway through a bowling spell at Nottingham and then, the showman that he is, promptly taking a wicket), while coach Brendon McCullum received the tap on the shoulder. Bazball done.

Now we have reset 2.0 with a new skipper - and an old one, too, with Joe Root retaking the job he previously held from 2017-2022 - and a new permanent coach, although not straight away with Stephen Fleming only taking over in earnest ahead of the South Africa trip this winter, leaving Marcus Trescothick in interim charge against Pakistan from Wednesday, live on Sky Sports.

For good or for bad, we knew how England's Bazballers would approach a Test match but with Baz and Ben now gone - the former moving into international retirement, the latter focusing on his role as white-ball head coach - it will be intriguing to see how the style evolves in Root's second term at the helm.

How will England look to play under Root?

Root stressed to Sky Sports' Michael Atherton that he did not want to be seen as a "negative captain" after the issue of England not appearing to even attempt a chase of 273 against New Zealand at Lord's under his leadership in 2021 was brought up - Dom Sibley's dead-batted 60 off 207 balls highlighted that mindset.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root revealed to Sky Sports' Michael Atherton that he has scrapped England's midnight curfew

He spoke glowingly about the effect Bazball had on "taking the fear away" from players and how much he had enjoyed being part of it. He plans to take that into his latest stint as leader but also bring a bit more situational awareness.

In one of Stokes' first interviews as captain four years ago, he was adamant he would never play for a draw. Root, though, explained to Atherton that his England would understand when that was sometimes the way to go. It seems a bit of nuance is coming.

And that is all England fans and followers have been crying out for.

Bazball was not inherently bad, in fact it was inherently good in lifting the team out of the funk they were in after a long period of poor results and oppressive Covid bubbles beforehand.

But it was also inherently flawed and never really sustainable. Root's job now is to channel the best bits of Bazball, add his own stamp and build a winning machine. If England can play as Root bats, then they probably won't go far wrong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Go back to England's second Test against Pakistan at Emirates Old Trafford in 2016 as Root scored 254

You could never accuse Root of being negative with the blade - we often hear pundits mention how you look up and England's all-time leading run-scorer is on 30 from 30 balls or similar - but he knows when to dial things down and how to win games.

Time for England to start winning again

Winning is not something England are too familiar with in Test cricket at the moment. Their implosion against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June means they have lost seven and won just two of their last 10 matches. Both of those wins came in two-day toss-ups.

Victories also eluded England during the final part of Root's first spell in charge, with just one across 17 matches before he left in April 2022 but it is worth remembering how taxing that Covid period was and that he didn't always have his best players available.

Root may never be a tactical genius, may not have the gutfeel Stokes had for captaincy - the failed short-ball barrage he deployed against New Zealand while standing in for Stokes at The Oval earlier this summer, dubbed "brainless" by Atherton, was a howler.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain feels Root sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader

Yet he is England's winning-most captain ever, with 27 victories, one more than Michael Vaughan and three more than Stokes and Sir Alastair Cook.

Plus, he feels time has made him realise what he does and does not need to get involved in as skipper and that he must not over-bowl a prized asset in Jofra Archer, something he admitted he was perhaps guilty of in the past.

There is a fear that Root's run-scoring could diminish with the added pressures of captaincy but that did not happen during the Covid era when he had the weight of the world on his shoulders, so it probably won't now either.

Root was not the sexiest choice to be England captain - Sky Sports' Mark Butcher called going back to him "retrograde" and it hardly speaks volumes about succession planning.

However, with Harry Brook's nightclub incident late last year still pretty fresh and Jacob Bethell remaining very nascent in his Test career, and injured now anyway, Root's appointment makes sense.

Image: Stokes (right) will be a big miss for England as they move forward in Test cricket under Root (left)

Stokes retirement leaves big void to fill

He has so many attributes to make this work, including previous experience and the complete respect of his team-mates, but what he doesn't have is Stokes.

Replacing Stokes in the XI is one thing - Dan Lawrence will do it against Pakistan, Sam Curran or Rehan Ahmed could do it in the future. Replacing his aura, all-round aptitude and ability to dig England out of a hole time and time again is almost impossible.

While maybe not the player he was, Stokes' departure means England are worse off.

The feeling, either genuine or just because it would be one hell of a story, is that Stokes could return for The Ashes next summer, a series England will be looking to win for the first time since 2015. Stokes says he won't but it would be no surprise if he did.

For now, though, England need to forget about Stokes and forget about The Ashes. The time has come to win again, starting against Pakistan. Let the new era begin - without the old mistakes.

Sports.title: Sky Sports and The Fast and the Curious announce new partnership
Sports.content:
Sky Sports and The Fast and the Curious have announced a new long-term strategic partnership, ahead of Formula 1's return to action this weekend with the Dutch Grand Prix.

Since launching in 2023, The Fast and the Curious has built a passionate and engaged community by making Formula 1 accessible, entertaining and inclusive. Hosted by Betty Glover, Christian Hewgill and Greg James, the podcast has become known for combining expert insight, exclusive interviews and behind-the-scenes access with humour, warmth and genuine curiosity.

The result is a show that helps new fans feel at home in Formula 1 while offering established followers a fresh perspective on the sport they love.

The overarching goal of the partnership is to help more people discover and enjoy Formula 1 by combining The Fast and the Curious' distinctive editorial voice with Sky Sports' world-class Formula 1 coverage and access.

The partnership will create further opportunities to tell the stories behind the sport, connect fans with the personalities who shape it and bring listeners closer to the action than ever before.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Don't miss the F1 season restart, which kicks off from Friday with the Dutch Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1

Billy McGinty, Sky Sports director of F1, said: "We are always looking to innovate so this partnership offers something genuinely new and exciting for Sky Sports.

"Alongside unlocking commercial benefits, Greg, Betty and Christian have a brilliant ability to relate to the everyday fan, so it presents a great opportunity on both sides to reach new audiences and grow fandom together."

Greg James, 'team principal' of The Fast and the Curious, added: "This is a very large mid-season upgrade! Adding a Sky Sports power unit to our podcast is so exciting.

"When we started The Fast and the Curious, my aim was to create the kind of Formula 1 podcast I've always wanted to listen to; one that was knowledgeable without being intimidating, entertaining without taking itself too seriously, and welcoming to everyone, particularly new fans who wanted to find their gang.

"Partnering with Sky Sports gives us the opportunity to build on everything we've created so far while staying true to what makes the podcast special. We can't wait to see where we can take the show together."

The partnership will bring cross-promotional opportunities with collaborative social posts and the inclusion of The Fast and The Curious content within Sky's digital ecosystem.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See what some of the Formula 1 drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

For OG listeners of The Fast and the Curious podcast, the things they love won't change. Betty, Christian and Greg will continue to bring their unique chemistry, curiosity and passion for Formula 1 to every episode.

One of the podcast's calling cards has been to have F1 drivers on as regular co-hosts. Whether it's finding out that Kimi Antonelli was still at school, learning that Ollie Bearman almost committed 'credit card fraud' (the hosts pretended to have him removed from Silverstone by security as a result) or the more serious discussion with Lewis Hamilton about his desire to make sure LGBTQ+ people feel welcomed by the sport, the gang will continue to unearth new sides of the biggest names on the grid.
